newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish metal firms among front runners for Ibex-35.
newsitem.headline: Spanish metal firms among front runners for Ibex-35.

text.p: Spanish metal companies Asturiana del Zinc and Tubacex have secured a place among front runners to join Spain's Ibex-35 index of leading shares when it is revised in July, analysts said on Tuesday.

Although the exact criteria used to select component companies remain a guarded secret, analysts believe market capitalisation and liquidity are two likely pointers, and the two firms have performed impressively in these fields.
Shares in leading zinc producer Asturiana have almost doubled in price since the beginning of the year, boosted by a cyclical upturn in zinc prices and strength in the dollar, dealers said.
"Zinc has been a late recovery product and it is a product that is traded in dollars," said Benito Vera, a Spain equity analyst at Salomon Brothers in London.
"This is pushing the company from big losses to big profits in a matter of months and this is why the share price has performed so well this year," he added.
Asturiana posted a net attributable loss of 2.65 billion pesetas in 1996 largely based on a loss-making futures position which it cleared.
However, it said earlier this year that it expected to swing to profit in 1997 and post a net attibutable profit of 5.0 billion pesetas based on a zinc price of between $1,050 and $1,030 per tonne.
But zinc prices may far exceed the company's most optimistic expectations, analysts said.

Three-month zinc futures were trading around $1,365 on the London Metals Exchange on Tuesday after touching 4-1/2 year highs of $1,377 last Friday and gaining more than 25 percent since the start of the year.
Meanwhile, the dollar has stormed from levels of around 125 pesetas at the beginning of the year to current levels around 145 pesetas.
Another factor boosting the liquidity of Asturiana's stock was the sale in February of Banesto's 24.79 percent stake to Glencore, analysts said.
Although liquidity will remain elevated, analysts said they did not expect Asturiana's share price to sustain the sharp rises seen so far this year.
"The share price is likely to remain fairly flat into the end of the year with zinc prices and the dollar unlikely to perform as strongly as we've seen so far," said one analyst.
Asturiana's share price has risen from a level of 1,250 pesetas in January to trade around 2,480 pesetas on Tuesday.
Analysts believe steel tube producer Tubacex is also well placed to join the index, its share price having gained more than 30 percent since the beginning of the year.
Tubacex's success has not so much been based on its commodity price, but rather a successful restructuring policy, analysts said.
"Tubacex's case is more a recovery story and the company has gone through a long and painful restructuring process and now its in a very competitive position," said Vera.
Other analysts cited dollar strength, Tubacex being a prime exporter, and lower interest rates as key factors underlying its success this year.
Tubacex shares have risen from a level of 250 pesetas in January to trade at levels around 330 pesetas on Tuesday.

The constituent companies of the Ibex index are reassessed twice yearly in January and July by a committee made up of five representatives from the Stock Exchange authority, the MEFF futures exchange and market experts. The committee does not make public the criteria it uses.
